newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Libya's Gaddafi says Turkish army run by Jews.
newsitem.headline: Libya's Gaddafi says Turkish army run by Jews.

text.p: Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi on Wednesday attacked the Turkish army for its incursion against Kurdish bases in northern Iraq and its military cooperation with Israel, saying it was ruled by Jews.
"The Jews who rule the Turkish army made it (take a stand) against the Arabs," Gaddafi said in a speech in the Libyan city of Derna broadcast by Libyan television and monitored in Tunis.
"It (the army) is ruled by a Jewish sect called Durma and which joined the Moslem religion by hypocrisy," he added at a rally attended by thousands of people. .
"Poor elected (Turkey's Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin) Erbakan, he wasn't aware that his army had entered Iraq...this is a mascarade," Gaddafi said.
Thousands of Turkish troops poured into northern Iraq on May 14 in pursuit of Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) guerrillas fighting for an independent Kurdish state in southeastern Turkey.
Most Arab states protested against the Turkish incursion, calling for the respect of integrity and unity of Iraqi territory.
The Arab countries were also worried about a Turkish-Israeli defence pact signed by the two states in recent months.

Last year Erbakan made a controversial visit to Libya which stirred criticism both in Turkey and in Washington. He led a 120-strong delegation including businessmen and members of parliament from all political parties.
